test.name: 1880+ census: stated relationship-to-head is direct evidence, not inferred
test.description: Converted from ut_record_extraction_018: the record the user pasted is now served as a record_read fixture (the 1900 census household of George Bennett, Springfield, Illinois, with its relationship-to-head column), and extraction runs in code. Extract from a 1900 census household. Unlike the 1850/1860 census, the 1900 census HAS a relationship-to-head column, so each person's relationship to the head is STATED by the record, not inferred from household position. The parent-child relationship (head/wife -> the stated 'Son') and the spousal relationship (head <-> the stated 'Wife') are therefore DIRECT evidence. The agent must NOT downgrade a stated 'Son'/'Daughter'/'Wife' to indirect on the grounds that a household relationship isn't necessarily biological parentage — from 1880 on the record STATES the relationship, and stated = direct. Mirrors the applegarth-parents-1936 e2e run, where the agent classified a 1940-census stated 'son' as indirect. From senior-genealogist (Shaunese) + Dallan review.

judge_context: The skill makes one extraction_append call with the record id and relays each record's summary verbatim. Grade that call and that relay; the classifications are decided in code and are checked by the expected_classifications validator, not by you.
The test hands the skill this record; whether it bears on the project's research objective or names the project's people is not graded.
